title: Distance Is How Often Crossovers Separate

scenes.tts: Cross a fruit fly with two mutations to a fly with only recessive alleles. Mendel's law of independent assortment predicts that five hundred of a thousand offspring look like one grandparent or the other. You count eight hundred and thirty. Something is holding those alleles together. Genes that lie near each other on one chromosome are called linked.
scenes.visual: 1,000 offspring as a grid of dots: 500 light up for Mendel's prediction, then 830 are counted; the grid gives way to two loci close together on one chromosome, labelled linked.
scenes.narration: Cross a fruit fly with two mutations to a fly with only recessive alleles. Mendel's law of independent assortment predicts that five hundred of a thousand offspring look like one grandparent or the other. You count eight hundred and thirty. Something is holding those alleles together. Genes that lie near each other on one chromosome are called linked.

scenes.tts: Take two loci, A and B, each a gene's place on a chromosome. Our fly is a female. She got dominant big A and big B on one chromosome, and recessive little a and little b on the other. The tester gives only little a and little b. So each offspring shows which alleles came in her gamete, and counting offspring counts her gametes.
scenes.visual: The female's two chromosomes (A B and a b) and the tester's; a gamete from her meets the tester's a b gamete and the offspring reads out her allele combination.
scenes.narration: Take two loci, A and B, each a gene's place on a chromosome. Our fly is a female. She got dominant A and B on one chromosome, and recessive a and b on the other. The tester gives only a and b. So each offspring shows which alleles came in her gamete, and counting offspring counts her gametes.

scenes.tts: Each chromosome has copied itself into two sister chromatids, and the partners pair side by side. Here, one crossover falls between the two loci and swaps matching segments of two non sister chromatids. Those two chromatids now carry new combinations of alleles. So one crossover gives two recombinant products and two parental ones. The farther apart two loci lie, the more often a crossover falls between them.
scenes.visual: Four chromatids; a crossover swaps the right-hand ends of two non-sister chromatids; two are tagged recombinant, two parental; then near loci versus far loci show how often crossovers fall between them.

scenes.tts: In our cross, the two parental classes hold four hundred twenty and four hundred ten flies. That is eight hundred thirty parental flies. The two recombinant classes hold eighty five flies each. So one hundred seventy of a thousand flies are recombinant, which is seventeen percent. One percent recombinant offspring is one centimorgan, so these loci are seventeen centimorgans apart.
scenes.visual: Four bars rise: 420 A B and 410 a b in green, 85 A b and 85 a B in red; the totals become 170 over 1,000, 17 percent, 17 cM.
scenes.narration: In our cross, the two parental classes hold four hundred twenty and four hundred ten flies. That is eight hundred thirty parental flies. scenes.tts: Recombination frequency never passes fifty percent. One crossover involves only two of the four chromatids, so it gives half recombinant products. A second crossover can put the loci back, so long intervals are underestimated. Haldane's function corrects for this, assuming that crossovers form independently of one another. It turns our seventeen percent into about twenty point eight centimorgans.
scenes.visual: Four chromatids with two swapped give half recombinant; a second crossover restores the loci; a plot of recombination frequency against distance flattens under a 50 percent ceiling, and Haldane's curve places 17 percent at about 20.8 cM.

scenes.tts: This female received big A with little b on one chromosome, and little a with big B on the other. She still gives seventeen percent recombinants. But now they are big A big B and little a little b, eight and a half percent each. Big A little b and little a big B are parental, forty one and a half percent each. The parents define the classes, not the counts, so read them first, then map with short intervals.
scenes.visual: The female now has A b and a B chromosomes; the four class bars show 41.5, 41.5, 8.5, 8.5 percent with the parental and recombinant colours flipped.
